# Handling web duplication

Day 2, 11:55 · John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead · coverage: transcript, slides

Speaker from the next talk's back-reference ('pick up where John left off with the canonical links'), heard in a second attendee recording.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Google deduplicates pages because many sites have very many pages and Google's index does not have room for everything.
  <br><sub>`D2-C344` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D1-C037](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Repeated by [D2-C680](D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's deduplication has three steps: identify and cluster duplicate web pages, pick representative URLs and index the unique pages, and forward signals to the representative URLs.
  <br><sub>`D2-C345` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Extends [D1-C128](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D1-C207](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extended by [D2-C701](D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For deduplication, a cluster is a set of pages Google considers essentially equivalent: Google stores one of them in the index and keeps track of the other related URLs.
  <br><sub>`D2-C346` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D1-C207](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Used by the glossary term *Duplicate cluster*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's speaker said what SEOs call the canonical is, for Google, the representative of a cluster of duplicate pages: the URL Google would ideally show.
  <br><sub>`D2-C347` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by the glossary term *Canonical*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google forwards the signals attached to every URL in a duplicate cluster, such as links, to the representative URL, so that nothing is lost by showing only one URL.
  <br><sub>`D2-C348` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Extends [D1-C111](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Contradicted by [D2-C429](D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Used by the glossary term *Canonical*</sub>

- **[Stage]** The first reason Google deduplicates is that users do not want to see the same page repeated in the search results, even if site owners would like it to rank ten times on page one.
  <br><sub>`D2-C349` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [A guide to Google Search ranking systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Storage is a second reason for deduplication: Google's storage has many competing uses and storage prices have risen sharply, so the space for any one use is limited and Google has to draw a line somewhere.
  <br><sub>`D2-C350` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google treats a site migration as deduplication across sites, in which the site owner says the old and the new domain are the same and that Google should pick the new domain, so deduplication also helps Google handle migrations.
  <br><sub>`D2-C351` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Extended by [D3-C642](D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google keeps the other URLs of a duplicate cluster as 'alternate names': equivalent URLs with the same content that Google still tracks as alternate versions of the representative URL.
  <br><sub>`D2-C352` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Used by the glossary term *Alternate names*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Alternate names also serve localization: if Google knows that country versions such as you.de and you.at are equivalent, it can pick the right version to show using hreflang.
  <br><sub>`D2-C353` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Alternate names are why a site: query for an old domain still shows the old domain's URLs after a site migration, which site owners often misread as a migration that is not working.
  > "FYI "alternate names" is why you see old domains in site:-queries"
  <br><sub>`D2-C354` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** When someone searches for an old domain after a migration, Google shows the old URL as an alternate version because that is what was searched for, and relies on the redirect to take the user to the new site.
  <br><sub>`D2-C355` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`</sub>

- **[Slide]** After a rebrand that changes the domain (the slide's example was johns-bikes to slow-bikes), Google can still show the old domain to people who search for the old brand by name, in navigational and branded queries.
  <br><sub>`D2-C356` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's redirects guide says Google keeps track of both the source and the target of a redirect: one becomes the canonical, depending on signals such as whether the redirect is permanent or temporary, and the other becomes an alternate name that may appear in results when a query suggests the user trusts the old URL more. After a move to a new domain, old URLs may still show occasionally; the guide calls this normal.
  > "This is normal and as users get used to the new domain name, the alternate names will fade away without you doing anything."
  <br><sub>`D2-C357` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`, `DEV-CAN-09`, the glossary term *Alternate names*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** After a migration, judge success by the new domain's indexing and traffic in Search Console rather than by a site: query on the old domain, and keep the old domain's redirects in place long term so searches for the old brand still reach the new site.
  <br><sub>`D2-C358` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's duplication talk described three related parts of deduplication: building clusters, localization, and selecting the representative URL, which is the canonicalization site owners see in Search Console.
  <br><sub>`D2-C359` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [URL Inspection tool](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google builds duplicate clusters from four kinds of input: redirects, content, rel=canonical, and a 'magic bucket' of other things.
  <br><sub>`D2-C360` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google trusts redirects very much for clustering, because a redirect is a clear sign that there is one version of the content; Google keeps track of both URLs but stores only one copy of the content.
  <br><sub>`D2-C361` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Whether a redirect is permanent or temporary matters only for choosing the canonical, not for clustering the URLs together.
  > "the permanent redirect really only matters for canonicalization, not for clustering."
  <br><sub>`D2-C362` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Use permanent redirects (301 or 308) for moves you want reflected in Search: a temporary redirect still groups the URLs, but it changes which URL Google is likely to pick as the canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C363` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google clusters duplicate pages by content in four ways: exact matches, near matches, structurally similar content, and soft 404s.
  <br><sub>`D2-C364` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Exact-match duplicates, such as the www and non-www versions of the same page, are clustered and Google keeps only one of them.
  <br><sub>`D2-C365` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by `DEV-CAN-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Pages whose boilerplate, such as menu and footer, is translated while the main content is not are near matches: the main reason to visit is the same, so Google clusters them as duplicates.
  > "When main content is the same, pages may be clustered."
  <br><sub>`D2-C366` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions) · Used by `DEV-INT-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Soft 404 pages are another reason Google clusters pages together, an outcome site owners usually do not want.
  <br><sub>`D2-C367` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extends [D1-C073](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google sometimes picks a canonical that looks unrelated because it recognised a URL pattern: if /buy/fax, /buy/typewriter and /office-equipment show the same content, its systems may assume any /buy/ URL, even /buy/seo-service, shows that same office-equipment content without looking at the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C368` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's slide on structurally similar content asked whether a new URL that fits a known duplicate pattern, such as /buy/seo-service, even needs to be crawled.
  > "Do we even need to crawl /buy/seo-service ?"
  <br><sub>`D2-C369` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C128](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D1-C094](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Slide]** City pages can trigger the same pattern-based deduplication: for a car dealer brand with branches in several cities and similar stock, Google's systems may decide the city name does not matter and canonicalise to one city's page; the slide asked whether a further city page such as /zurich/services would be treated the same way.
  <br><sub>`D2-C370` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** To avoid pattern-based deduplication, Google's speaker recommended not having many unrelated, similar-looking URLs that lead to the same content, and returning error pages for URLs that no longer exist so they are clearly unrelated.
  > "Misleading site structure (use clear signals!)"
  <br><sub>`D2-C371` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [Troubleshoot Google Search crawling errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Make location and variant pages differ in their main content (local stock, staff, prices, addresses) and return 404 for empty or invalid combinations; otherwise every URL that fits the pattern can be folded into one canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C372` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's canonicalization troubleshooting guide says fixing a wrong duplicate cluster comes down to making the clustered pages sufficiently different; pages split out faster when the difference is clear and significant, and Google may keep pages in a duplicate cluster for up to two weeks after a fix.
  <br><sub>`D2-C373` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A growing cause of wrong clustering is bot protection: when a CDN or another protection system shows Googlebot the same 'you look like a bot, solve this puzzle' page on many unrelated URLs or domains, Google can cluster those pages as duplicates.
  <br><sub>`D2-C374` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns), [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Extends [D1-C069](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extends [D1-C078](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extends [D1-C367](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's systems find it very hard to recognise a bot-challenge page as an error page, and Googlebot cannot solve the puzzles, such as selecting all the cats, that those pages ask for.
  <br><sub>`D2-C375` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extends [D1-C367](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Search Central post on CDNs says that if Google cannot recognise an error message served with a 200 status as an error, all pages showing the same message may be dropped from the index as duplicates, and recovery can be slow because Google has little incentive to recrawl duplicates. For bot-verification interstitials it recommends sending crawlers a 503 status.
  <br><sub>`D2-C376` · Search Central blog (24 December 2024) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extends [D1-C078](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-03`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** AI agents that browse the web for users run into the same bot walls that sites put up against scrapers, and may give up and go to another site, for example to buy the product elsewhere.
  <br><sub>`D2-C377` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C436](D1-S12-q-a.md) · Used by `DEV-AIF-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Check what your CDN or bot protection serves to verified Googlebot and to the AI agents you want to allow; if crawlers must get a challenge page, return it with a 503 status as Google recommends, never as a 200 page across many URLs, which Google may cluster as duplicates.
  <br><sub>`D2-C378` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Used by `DEV-AIF-04`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** rel=canonical is probably the most common way site owners signal duplicates, but it is very often wrong, for example a tag whose value reads 'canonical target' instead of a real URL (the example is partly unclear in the recording), so Google can only sometimes trust it.
  <br><sub>`D2-C379` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical) · Extends [D2-C031](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Many SEOs assume Google must follow their rel=canonical, but because people sometimes get it wrong, Google has to make its own judgment about the canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C380` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Extends [D1-C113](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Repeated by [D2-C402](D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Used by the glossary term *rel=canonical*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Same-language content for different countries is tricky for Google's deduplication, notably German pages for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and possibly Spanish-language variants.
  <br><sub>`D2-C381` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/managing-multi-regional-sites) · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** When localized pages are clustered, Google tries to use hreflang alternates; the speaker's short version of the advice was to use hreflang, which he called really helpful for same-language, different-country content.
  > "We try to use hreflang alternates."
  <br><sub>`D2-C382` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Extends [D2-C033](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's speaker advised against 'clever' geo-redirecting, because it very often goes wrong.
  > "clever" geo-redirecting (is often not so clever)"
  <br><sub>`D2-C383` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/managing-multi-regional-sites) · Used by `DEV-INT-02`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For German-language sites serving Germany, Austria and Switzerland, add hreflang with region codes (de-DE, de-AT, de-CH) and make the country pages differ in more than boilerplate (prices, shipping, legal details), or expect Google to cluster them and show one.
  <br><sub>`D2-C384` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's canonical guide says that for canonicalization Google prefers URLs that are part of hreflang clusters: if German pages for Germany and Switzerland point to each other with hreflang but not to the Austrian page, the German and Swiss pages are preferred as canonicals.
  <br><sub>`D2-C385` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google picks the canonical from a variety of criteria and uses some kind of machine learning to decide how much weight each criterion gets; the weighting changes from time to time.
  > "we use some kind of machine learning to understand how strong these criteria should be. And this changes from time to time."
  <br><sub>`D2-C386` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google named three considerations when picking a representative URL: hijacking across pages or sites, user experience (the page can load, meta refresh, security) and site-owner signals (redirects, rel=canonical, sitemaps).
  <br><sub>`D2-C387` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls), [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`, `DEV-CAN-02`, `DEV-CAN-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google watches for canonical hijacking, where several domains try to be canonical for the same content, whether accidentally across a site owner's own domains (such as a staging copy) or through third-party domains, maliciously or not, and asks site owners to report cases it gets wrong.
  <br><sub>`D2-C388` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by `DEV-CAN-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Whether a page can load is really important for canonical selection: a broken certificate, failing JavaScript or a page that cannot be loaded counts against a URL, and the slide also listed meta refresh and security.
  <br><sub>`D2-C389` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Clear site-owner signals about which URL should be canonical make a big difference to Google's choice; the speaker named redirects, listing only the preferred URL in sitemaps, and rel=canonical, which the speaker said also helps a bit.
  <br><sub>`D2-C390` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls), [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`, `DEV-URL-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's canonical guide ranks the ways to signal a preferred canonical by strength: redirects and rel=canonical annotations are strong signals, sitemap inclusion is a weak signal, and combining methods makes them more effective.
  <br><sub>`D2-C391` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`, `DEV-URL-05`, the glossary term *rel=canonical*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's duplication talk described rel=canonical as something that 'also helps a bit', while Google's canonical guide calls it a strong signal alongside redirects and calls sitemap inclusion weak; treat redirects and rel=canonical as the main levers and sitemaps as support.
  <br><sub>`D2-C392` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's speaker said that pointing rel=canonical from the pages of a paginated set to the first page can sometimes make sense depending on the goal, for example to make a category page more visible, but that it affects canonicalization and deduplication.
  <br><sub>`D2-C393` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Contradicts [D1-C115](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's pagination guide still says not to use page 1 as the canonical of a paginated series, so keep self-referencing canonicals on paginated pages unless you deliberately want later pages folded into page 1 and the items they list are linked from elsewhere.
  <br><sub>`D2-C394` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's 2013 post on rel=canonical mistakes says pointing rel=canonical from page 2 or later of a paginated series to page 1 is incorrect because the pages are not duplicates, and that it would result in the content on later pages not being indexed at all.
  <br><sub>`D2-C395` · Search Central blog (8 April 2013) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical) · Extends [D1-C115](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's closing suggestions on duplication: use redirects for site migrations, use HTTP result codes, don't block agents, check your rel=canonical links, use hreflang links to help Google localize, report weird canonicals in the forums, make secure pages that work, and keep canonical signals clear.
  <br><sub>`D2-C396` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls), [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes), [Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions), [Troubleshoot Google Search crawling errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) · Extended by [D2-C882](D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's duplication talk closed with the advice not to block agents, which the speaker said are sometimes really cool.
  > "Don't block agents."
  <br><sub>`D2-C397` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C131](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-AIF-04`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's speaker suggested checking rel=canonical links with a crawler such as Screaming Frog to make sure they are reasonable.
  <br><sub>`D2-C398` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D2-C408](D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** When all canonical signals point to the same URL, Google follows what the site owner says; when they point in different directions, Google cannot tell what the owner wants.
  > "if there are multiple things in different directions, we don't know what to do."
  <br><sub>`D2-C399` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Before a migration or template change, align every canonical signal for the preferred URL (redirects, rel=canonical, internal links, sitemap entries, hreflang and working HTTPS); Google says it follows the site owner only when the signals agree.
  <br><sub>`D2-C400` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's pagination guide says the pages of a paginated sequence may share the same title and description, and suggests linking every page of the sequence back to the first page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C832` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>
